correctness.rationale: Gaussian completion of squares yields both independent-detector marginals and their product exactly. The derivative in squared detector separation factors into a positive term times one strictly decreasing exponential minus one; all boundary/equality cases and global uniqueness follow. The logarithmic derivative of critical baseline quality has exactly one positive turning point for d>2 and is negative for d<=2, proving the sharp spatial-dimension barrier and unique critical root; a controlled large-d expansion gives the stated asymptotics. Extracted standard-library checker passed 86,581 deterministic assertions, with independent one-dimensional quadrature; numerical evidence is not used as a continuum proof.

evidence: For independent conditional detections, at-least-one capture equals the sum of the two mean detection probabilities minus their joint mean; the signed derivative of this explicit two-exponential function completely controls optimum spacing.

The planar special case is already known and is excluded from the new priority claim; that case does not imply a nonzero all-quality co-location interval in dimension three.

value.rationale: Three-dimensional animal utilization is materially different from a flattened planar model: this classification supplies a new impossibility interval, in which separating two identical independent detectors is never optimal even at baseline probability one. This is a structural phase transition at the first physical volumetric dimension, with exact 3D cutoff, golden-ratio 4D cutoff and high-dimensional exponential scaling. The objectively relevant at-least-once detection event differs from commonly optimized estimator precision; the theorem is limited to a mathematically motivated symmetric design and does not assert field validity.
